title: How to Create Multiple Ads on Facebook: 4 Methods and When to Use Each
summary: Four ways to create multiple Facebook ads: duplicate, add ads to an ad set, dynamic creative or flexible ads, and bulk import. When each one fits and its limits.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- There are four ways to create multiple Facebook ads in Ads Manager: **duplicate** an ad, **add several ads** to one ad set, use **dynamic creative or flexible ads** so Meta combines your assets, or **bulk import** from a spreadsheet.
- For a handful of variations, add ads to one ad set. It takes minutes and gives clean, readable results.
- To test many images, headlines and texts at once without managing each ad, use dynamic creative or flexible ads.
- For dozens of ads, such as one per product or per audience, use the spreadsheet import.
- More ads is not better. Too many ads in one ad set splits spend too thin for any of them to learn.


Testing is how Meta advertising improves, and testing means more than one ad. Ads Manager gives you several ways to build variations, and picking the wrong one wastes either time or budget. Here is each method, the steps, and when it is the right call. Menus and labels shift as Meta updates Ads Manager, so treat the steps as the shape of the process.


## First, the structure


Meta organizes ads in three levels: **campaigns** (the objective), **ad sets** (audience, budget, placements and schedule) and **ads** (the creative). Multiple ads usually live inside one ad set, sharing its budget and audience. Meta's delivery system then shifts spend toward the ads it expects to perform.


That is useful, and it has a catch. Delivery picks favorites early, so an ad can get most of the spend before a fair test has happened. Plan for it, as covered below.


## Method 1: Duplicate an existing ad


Best when you have a working ad and want a variant, such as a new headline or image.


1. In Ads Manager, open the **Ads** tab and select the ad.
2. Click **Duplicate** . Choose to keep the copy in the same ad set, or put it in another.
3. Edit the copy. Change one element only, so you know what caused any difference.
4. Publish.


**Use it for:** quick tests of one change. **Avoid it for:** building 20 variants by hand, which is slow and error-prone.


## Method 2: Add several ads to one ad set


This is the default way to run a creative test and it is hard to beat.


1. Create or open the ad set.
2. At the ad level, add a second and third ad. Each gets its own image or video, text, headline and call to action.
3. Name them clearly, such as` Hook-Problem_v1` and` Hook-Social-proof_v1` .
4. Publish and let them run before judging.


**Use it for:** three to six ads with distinct ideas. Each ad stays visible in reports, so you can read the winner directly. **Avoid it for:** trying every combination of image and text. That is what the next method does.


## Method 3: Dynamic creative or flexible ads


Here you give Meta a pool of assets and it assembles the ads.


1. At the ad set level, turn on **dynamic creative** , or choose the **flexible** ad format at the ad level, depending on what your account shows.
2. Upload several images or videos. Add multiple primary texts, headlines and descriptions. Meta's limits on how many of each you can add apply, so check the count in the interface.
3. Meta mixes them and learns which combinations get results.
4. Review the asset-level breakdown to see which images and texts worked.


**Use it for:** finding which headline, text and image combine well when you have no strong prior, and for small budgets where a dozen separate ads would starve. **Avoid it for:** tests where the message must stay together, such as a before-and-after story, because Meta may pair a headline with an image that contradicts it. Results are also harder to read than separate ads, because you see asset performance, not whole-ad performance.


Meta also offers its Advantage+ creative enhancements, which make automatic edits to your ads. Review them, since they can change how your brand looks.


## Method 4: Bulk import from a spreadsheet


For large volumes, Ads Manager can import ads from a spreadsheet.


1. In Ads Manager, find the **Import and export** menu and choose to export a template, or **Create and edit multiple ads** .
2. Download the template file. It has columns for campaign, ad set and ad details such as names, URLs, text, image or video references and targeting.
3. Fill one row per ad. Use the same campaign and ad set names to put ads in the same group.
4. Upload the file and fix any rows Meta flags as errors.
5. Review the imported ads in Ads Manager before publishing.


**Use it for:** one ad per product in a catalog, one per city, one per audience, or a large launch. **Avoid it for:** small tests, where the setup costs more than it saves. Check your ad naming first. Consistent names, such as` Product_Hook_Format_Date` , make the results sortable later.


Ecommerce brands with product catalogs may find catalog ads a better fit than hundreds of individual ads, since Meta builds an ad per product from the feed. The[Shopify Facebook ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/shopify-facebook-ads) guide covers that route.


## Which method to use


Situation Method


One working ad, one variation Duplicate


3 to 6 distinct ideas Several ads in one ad set


Many images and texts, no strong prior Dynamic creative or flexible ads


Dozens of ads from a list Spreadsheet import


A different audience for each ad Separate ad sets, not separate ads


## How many ads is too many?


Each ad set needs enough conversions to learn. Meta's delivery system generally needs a steady number of results per week for each ad set to leave its learning phase. If your budget produces a handful of conversions a week, forty ads in one ad set will not teach you anything. Start with three to five, kill the clear losers after they have had a fair run, and add new variations to replace them.


There is also a ceiling on the number of ads an ad account or Page can run. If you hit it, see[Meta's ad limit per ad account](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/meta-ad-limit-per-ad-account) . Meta's delivery has changed too, and rewards creative variety. The overview of how is on the[Meta Andromeda](https://www.sprites.ai/meta-andromeda) page.


## What to vary


Do not make multiple ads that are the same ad with a different button. Make them different ideas:


- **The hook:** problem, result, question, claim, customer quote.
- **The format:** talking head, demo, UGC, static, carousel.
- **The offer:** discount, bundle, guarantee, free shipping.


To get ideas from live ads, open competitors' pages in the[Meta ads library](https://www.sprites.ai/meta-ads-library) , with brand pages like[Glossier ads](https://www.sprites.ai/glossier-ads) and industry pages like[ecommerce ads](https://www.sprites.ai/ecommerce-ads) . Then use the method in[analyze competitor ads for winning hooks](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/analyze-competitor-ads-winning-hooks) to separate hooks from formats.

## Frequently asked questions


### How do I create multiple ads at once on Facebook?


Add several ads to one ad set, use dynamic creative so Meta combines your assets, or use Ads Manager's bulk import to create ads from a spreadsheet. For one variation of an existing ad, duplicate it.


### How many ads should I run in one ad set?


Three to five distinct ads is a sound start. More ads spread the budget thinner, so each takes longer to produce a readable result.


### What is the difference between dynamic creative and flexible ads?


Both let Meta combine your assets into ads. Dynamic creative is an ad set setting that mixes images, videos and text. Flexible ads are an ad format that holds a pool of media in one ad. Which one you see depends on your account.


### Can I bulk upload Facebook ads?


Yes. Ads Manager's import and export tools let you download a template, fill in a row per ad, and upload it to create many ads at once.


### Should I duplicate an ad or create a new one?


Duplicate when you are changing one thing in a working ad. Create a new ad when the idea, the format and the message are different.


### Does duplicating an ad reset its learning?


A duplicate is a new ad and starts fresh, though it may benefit from the ad set's existing learning if it sits in the same ad set. The original keeps its social proof, such as likes and comments, unless you duplicate with the same post.
